title: Posts and Vacancies in Higher Education
text:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau

Ministry of Education

Posts and Vacancies in Higher Education

प्रविष्टि तिथि:
29 JUL 2026 6:24PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Higher Education Institutions (CHEIs) under Ministry of Education  including Central Universities (CUs) and Centrally Funded Technical Institutions (CFTIs) such as  Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), and National Institutes of Technology (NITs) are statutory  autonomous organizations established under respective Central Acts of Parliament and governed  by provisions of the Acts/Statutes/Ordinances/Regulations made thereunder. As autonomous  institutions, faculty recruitment is done within the institutions itself, in accordance with their Acts and Regulations. The recruitment powers vests with the respective Board of Governors/Executive  Committee/Board of Management.

Occurring of vacancies and filling thereof is a continuous process. The vacancies arise due to  promotion, retirement, resignation, death, opening of new institutions, schemes or projects, and additional requirements on account of enhanced students’ strength and expansion of capacity in  existing institutions.

In August, 2021, all CHEIs under the Ministry of Education were requested to undertake a special drive to fill backlog vacancies in their institutions in Mission Mode. The CHEIs undertook special  recruitment drives to fill the vacancies including Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs). In September 2022, the Ministry of Education had also exhorted all the CHEIs to fill up the vacancies in Mission Mode. In October 2025, all the CHEIs have again been requested to fill up all the backlog vacancies in Mission Mode. From September 2022, all CHEIs have undertaken Mission Mode recruitment drive to fill the vacancies. Up to  23.05.2026 (i.e. the date of last Rozgar Mela), a total number of 32,114 posts (3,851 SC, 1,643 ST,  6,785 OBC, 1,191 EWS) have been filled up by all CHEIs, including 18,757 faculty positions (2,315  SC, 910 ST, 3,986 OBC, 568 EWS), in Mission Mode.

The number of PhD admissions at CHEIs is dynamic and varies across admission cycles based  on the availability of faculty supervisors, departmental requirements, and funding support. Further,  the availability of PhD positions changes with the Institute’s faculty strength. New faculty members create additional research supervision capacity, while the research scholars of faculty members who resign, retire, or are transferred are reassigned to other eligible supervisors as per  the Institute’s academic regulations. The number of PhD enrolment has increased from 1,17,301  (as per AISHE Report 2014-15) to 3,43,559 (as per AISHE Report 2023-24) marking a growth of 192.89 %.

This information was given by the Minister of State in the Ministry of Education, Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.
